originality.rationale: Direct inspection of full Németh–Németh 2015, Kyng–Rao–Sachdeva 2015, Yang–Barber 2017 and relevant 1997 linear approximation theorem yields no sharp data-to-fit Lipschitz modulus for the non-Hilbert isotonic metric projection on arbitrary finite posets. The 1998 Finzel–Li abstract guarantees Lipschitz existence for general polyhedral targets but contains no exact constant. Seven actual semantic database searches found no covering claim. Graph independence and graph-specific sharpness are not consequences of the scalar constant-vector line alone; strict positive-multiplier full-pooling stability is an additional argument. A plausible full-text historical source is inaccessible and remains a documented overlap risk.
residual_risks: The full text of Finzel–Li (1998), doi:10.1006/jmaa.1998.6120, could not be directly inspected; abstract-level evidence does not exclude an unadvertised isotonic sharp special case.
Unindexed pre-2016 literature, differently named stability parameters, or private unpublished mathematics could contain an equivalent statement; searches do not certify global uniqueness.

It exposes surprising independence from branching/edge structure and a genuine two-sided transition at the Hilbert exponent. Proving graph-adapted normal-cone sharpness adds mathematical content beyond a routine scalar mean calculation; the exact parameter is directly relevant for worst-case perturbation amplification.
